title: Arithmetic Progressions
tagline: Year 3 — nth term, sum of n terms, arithmetic mean, and AP word problems

introduction.overview: An arithmetic progression (AP) is a sequence in which every term is obtained by adding a fixed number, the common difference d, to the previous term. This chapter develops the nth-term and sum formulas, the properties of terms equidistant from the ends, three-term AP tricks, and standard word problems on instalments, seating rows and counting multiples.
introduction.placementRelevance: AP questions are among the most frequent number-series questions in company aptitude tests, often as "find the sum" or "how many terms" problems.
introduction.realWorldContext: Salary increments of a fixed amount, equal instalment increases and stacked seating all form arithmetic progressions.

learningObjectives: Find the sum of multiples in a range
Use middle-term and three-number AP tricks

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: In an AP, consecutive differences are equal. The mean of two terms equals the term midway between them.

coreDefinitions: First term a and common difference d.
Sum of n terms: Sₙ = n/2 [2a + (n − 1)d] = n(a + l)/2 where l is the last term.
Arithmetic mean of x and y: (x + y)/2.
Number of terms between a and l: (l − a)/d + 1.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: The sum of an AP is the number of terms times the average of the first and last terms, because equidistant terms from the two ends have the same sum.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Write a, d, and the last term, count the terms with (l − a)/d + 1, then multiply by the average of the first and last term.

mainNarrative: Find the 20th term of 7, 11, 15, …. Here a = 7 and d = 4, so T₂₀ = 7 + 19 × 4 = 83.
Sum of the first 20 terms: S₂₀ = 20/2 × (7 + 83) = 900.
Counting terms: how many numbers between 1 and 100 are divisible by 7? The AP is 7, 14, …, 98, so n = (98 − 7)/7 + 1 = 14. Their sum is 14 × (7 + 98)/2 = 735.
For three numbers in AP use a − d, a, a + d; their sum is 3a, which fixes the middle term immediately. For five numbers use a − 2d, a − d, a, a + d, a + 2d.
If Sₙ is given as a quadratic in n, the first term is S₁ and the common difference is the coefficient of n² times 2. For Sₙ = 3n² + 2n, a = 5 and d = 6.

deepDiveAspects.title: Equidistant terms
deepDiveAspects.content: In an AP, Tₖ + Tₙ₋ₖ₊₁ = a + l for every k, which gives the sum formula.

solvedExamples.title: nth term and sum
solvedExamples.question: For the AP 7, 11, 15, …, find the 20th term and the sum of 20 terms.

solvedExamples.title: Count multiples
solvedExamples.question: Find the sum of all multiples of 7 between 1 and 100.

solvedExamples.title: Three numbers in AP
solvedExamples.question: Three numbers in AP have sum 27 and product 693. Find them.
solvedExamples.conceptOrFormula: Use a − d, a, a + d.
solvedExamples.commonTrap: Taking a = 27/3 and d = 3 without the product.

shortcutMethods.title: Average × count

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Sum = number of terms × average of the first and last terms; the middle term of an odd-length AP equals the average.

rulesForApplication: Three numbers: a − d, a, a + d.

commonMistakes.whyItHappens: Not the largest multiple within the range.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: The sum must be n times a value between the first and last terms.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Compute the last term before the sum.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Counting multiples is an AP in disguise.
